source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Ajanta Pharma operates branded generics in Asia and Africa markets with no explicit China+1 or supply chain diversification narrative found in FY2025 disclosures. US generics business grew 9% YoY to ₹1,047 crore in FY25. Export-oriented growth is driven by organic market expansion in Asia/Africa/US rather than supply-chain diversification from China.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports contributed approximately 68% of revenue in FY2025. US generics ~22.5%, Asia branded ~25.6%, Africa ~19.9% of total revenue. FY25 total revenue ₹4,648 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme beneficiary status found for Ajanta Pharma in FY2025 disclosures. Company is primarily a branded formulations company focused on emerging markets and US generics.

china_plus_one.evidence: JB Chemicals' CDMO business grew 18.3% YoY in FY2025, driven by a strong order book from global pharma clients seeking supply diversification. The company focuses on India branded formulations, CDMO (export), and select international markets. Domestic and CDMO business constitute ~69% of revenues. No explicit China+1 language found in available disclosures, but CDMO export momentum indicates supply diversification demand.

inr_exposure.evidence: International business contributes approximately 42% of revenue including South Africa, Russia, US, and other branded generics markets. CDMO revenues are partly USD-denominated. FY2025 total revenue ₹3,918 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: No specific PLI scheme beneficiary status confirmed for JB Chemicals in available FY2025 disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Navin Fluorine received its largest-ever multi-year deal: a 7-year contract worth USD 410 million (~₹3,000 crore) to manufacture and supply a High-Performance Product (HPP) to a large global MNC. The company's CRAMS/CDMO segment grew strongly, driven by global pharma and agrochem companies seeking supply chain diversification away from China for specialty fluorochemicals. Export contribution reached 77% in Q4 FY25. The HPP contract is explicitly linked to customers' need for non-China specialty chemical sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials include fluorspar/fluorite and HF (hydrofluoric acid) with some indirect crude linkage. Specific % of revenue attributable to crude-linked raw materials not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Approximately 55% of FY2025 revenue from exports. CRAMS and specialty chemicals are predominantly export-oriented with USD/EUR-denominated contracts. Q4 FY25 export share was 77%.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme beneficiary status confirmed for Navin Fluorine in specialty chemicals or bulk drugs category in FY2025 disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: Aegis Logistics is a domestic India-only logistics company providing LPG import terminals, liquid chemical terminals, and gas distribution. No export business and no China+1 narrative applicable.

rural.evidence: Company operates LPG distribution across Tier 1, 2, and 3 urban cities and has 142 autogas stations over 10 states, but no specific rural revenue percentage disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt surged to ₹2,353 crore as of March 2025 from ₹1,432 crore a year earlier (+64%). Specific floating vs fixed rate split not available from public sources.

crude_exposure.evidence: Aegis Logistics is a pure-play logistics/terminal operator for LPG and liquid chemicals. Revenue is primarily fee-based (throughput/storage/handling charges). Company does not have direct crude-linked raw material cost exposure in the same sense as manufacturers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company normalizes EBITDA before Forex and hedging-related expenses, indicating active forex management. LPG is imported and priced in USD, creating some pass-through forex exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: Aegis Logistics imports LPG from international markets (USD-priced commodity) but operates as a logistics/terminal operator in INR. Revenue is primarily INR-denominated service fees.

pli_scheme.evidence: No PLI scheme applicability confirmed for Aegis Logistics.

china_plus_one.evidence: From Lupin's FY2025 investor meet transcript: 'Lupin's focus is on de-risking, whether from China or other single source entities, working to build agility into the system so that lead times continue to improve.' And: 'As countries and regions are de-risking from China, the US in particular is very focused on de-risking from China, and India is well positioned to leverage that opportunity on multiple fronts.' Lupin's API Plus business offers 'global customers credible, cost-effective, and high-quality solutions as the world seeks secure and diversified API sources.'

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Layered hedging strategy with natural hedges and forex derivatives. Treasury operations actively monitor exposures across USD-INR, EUR-INR, and ZAR-INR across 100+ markets.
inr_exposure.evidence: Operating in 100+ markets with US at 38% and total exports at 66% of total revenue. FY2025 total revenue ₹227 billion. Natural hedges and forex derivatives deployed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin was selected as one of 9 domestic pharmaceutical companies approved under the PLI scheme for the pharmaceutical sector. Global API sales were ₹11,772 crore (5% of global sales) in FY2025, up 3.1% YoY.

china_plus_one.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a domestic diagnostics chain with no material export business. No China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative is present in the FY2024-25 annual report.

rural.evidence: FY2024-25 annual report highlights aggressive Tier-3 and Tier-4 expansion. 18 new laboratories added in FY25 (total 280+), with explicit focus on underserved Tier-3/Tier-4 towns. Q2 FY25 revenue was 'driven by increased volumes, organic expansion, and strong performance in Tier-III and Tier-IV towns.' Exact rural revenue % not disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Government hospital contracts exist but no % disclosed. Company is a B2C and B2B diagnostics provider.

rate_sensitive.evidence: The company is effectively debt-free (Debt/Equity ratio = 0.0 in FY25). No meaningful floating-rate debt exposure disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Diagnostics is a services business. Key cost inputs are reagents, consumables, and laboratory supplies — not crude-linked commodities.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is almost entirely domestic India (INR). International presence limited to Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh (negligible).

pli_scheme.evidence: Dr Lal PathLabs is a diagnostics services company and does not participate in any PLI manufacturing scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Nestle India is a domestic-focused FMCG company. The annual report does not present a China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative. Exports are minimal (~2% of revenue). No China+1 framing present.

rural.evidence: FY2024-25 annual report discloses significant rural market focus: presence in ~208,500 villages. General Trade delivered strong double-digit growth 'led by rural markets.' Q3 FY25 press release noted 'robust performance across all town classes, led by rural markets.' Exact rural revenue % not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nestle India is a largely debt-free or low-debt company (FY25 revenue ~₹24,500 crore, net profit ~₹3,545 crore). Exact floating rate debt % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials include milk, wheat, cocoa, palm oil, and sugar — agricultural commodities partially correlated with crude (packaging, logistics) but not directly crude-linked. No specific crude-linked raw material % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Exports minimal (~2% of revenue). As part of Nestle global group, hedging policy exists but is not separately disclosed for the India entity.
inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue is overwhelmingly domestic India (INR). Limited USD/forex revenue from marginal exports. FY25 revenue ₹23,155 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nestle India received Government of India approval on December 6, 2021, under the PLI scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) for processed fruits and vegetables. Confirmed PLI beneficiary. Specific revenue % from PLI-linked products not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Torrent Pharma is primarily a branded generics company focused on India, Germany, Brazil, and the US. No explicit China+1 narrative attributing revenue growth to supply chain diversification is present. The company's export profile is branded generics, not CDMO/API manufacturing for Western pharma seeking to diversify away from China.

rural.evidence: India business (55% of revenue, ₹6,393 crore in FY25, up 13%) covers urban and semi-urban branded prescription drugs. Rural-specific revenue breakdown not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Long-term debt fell to ₹12 billion in FY25 from ₹16 billion in FY24 (down 25.7%). Interest coverage improved to 11.6x from 7.7x. Specific floating vs fixed rate split not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Pharma raw materials (APIs, solvents, excipients) have indirect crude linkage through petrochemical-derived solvents. No specific crude-linked raw material % disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company has a documented hedging policy for forex exposure given 45% of revenues are from exports (US, Germany, Brazil, other markets). Specific hedging instruments not disclosed in available summaries.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue breakdown: India 55% (~₹6,393 crore), US ~10% (~₹1,110 crore), Germany ~10%, Brazil ~10%, Other ~15%. Total FY25 revenue ₹11,516 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: Torrent Pharmaceuticals approved under the PLI scheme for pharmaceutical sector for domestic manufacturing of critical Key Starting Materials, Drug Intermediates, and APIs. Specific PLI-linked revenue % not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sai Life Sciences explicitly positions as a China+1 beneficiary. Investor materials state: 'Large pharma increasingly diversifies supply chains in a China+1 strategy, and CDMOs in India are stepping into a new era of opportunity.' The company serves 280+ innovator pharma and biotech companies across US, UK, Europe, and Japan seeking to diversify away from China. Overseas revenue: 97.95% in FY24, 97.40% in H1 FY25, 98.27% in FY23. The company explicitly frames its CRDMO positioning as capturing China+1 opportunity.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company carries debt for manufacturing capacity expansion and hedges forex exposure via forward contracts, currency swaps, call-put options, and interest rate swaps. Floating rate debt % not specifically disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Chemical synthesis involves solvents and reagents with some petrochemical linkage. CDMO contracts often allow pass-through of raw material costs. Specific % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Active hedging via forward contracts, currency swaps, call-put options, and interest rate swaps given ~98% of revenue is from overseas (primarily USD/EUR denominated).
inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue from overseas customers: 97.95% in FY24, 97.40% in H1 FY25, 98.27% in FY23. FY25 total revenue ~₹1,695 crore (up 16% YoY). Client base spans US, UK/Europe, Japan.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sai Life Sciences is a CDMO/CRO focused on innovative drug development services. No PLI beneficiary status found in disclosures.

china_plus_one.evidence: CCL Products is an instant coffee manufacturer and exporter. No China+1 supply chain diversification narrative present. Competitive moat is built on cost-efficient manufacturing and product quality, not geopolitical supply chain diversification. The company demonstrates supply chain agility (routing US volumes through Vietnam during tariff changes) but this is not framed as China+1.

rural.evidence: Domestic branded business ('Continental Coffee') ~₹210 crore in FY24 (~8% of revenue), expected to cross ₹300 crore in FY25 (~10% of revenue). Company targets increasing domestic B2C share to 50% of revenue by 2030. Rural market-specific revenue % not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: FY25 total debt ₹1,813 crore, of which ₹1,256 crore (~69%) is short-term debt backed by confirmed customer orders for green coffee inventory financing. Short-term working capital debt is typically floating rate. Exact floating rate % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is green (unroasted) coffee beans — an agricultural commodity NOT crude-linked. Coffee bean prices are driven by weather and supply from Brazil/Vietnam. No crude-linked raw material exposure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Natural hedge: ~75% of raw materials (green coffee beans) imported in USD, creating a natural hedge against USD-denominated export revenues. Management uses forward contracts and inventory hedging for coffee price risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: CCL Products derives 85-90% of revenue through exports across 110+ countries. Domestic branded business ('Continental Coffee') ~10-12% of revenue. ~75% of raw materials also imported in USD, creating a natural hedge. FY25 total revenue ~₹3,134 crore.

pli_scheme.evidence: Instant coffee is not a covered PLI category under PLISFPI (which covers RTE/RTC foods, processed fruits/vegetables, marine products, mozzarella cheese).

china_plus_one.evidence: ABSLAMC is a domestic Indian asset management company. All revenue is from management fees on India-domiciled AUM. No export business or supply chain diversification angle.

rate_sensitive.evidence: ABSLAMC has zero borrowings. Revenue is highly rate-sensitive via AUM mix: debt AUM yield ~25bp vs equity at 70-71bp. Management commentary: 'A marginal improvement is expected in fixed income yields with interest rate declining.' Debt AUM ~20% of total AAUM in FY25; equity+hybrid ~46%. Rate cuts benefit debt fund inflows and yields.

inr_exposure.evidence: ABSLAMC has offshore AUM of ₹127 billion (grew 28% YoY in Q3 FY25) managed through Mauritius subsidiary and GIFT City products. All domestic MF management fees are in INR. Offshore AUM contributes negligibly to revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: Bharat Forge is 'leveraging the China Plus One trend through capacity expansion in the United States and Europe to target local OEMs and reduce supply-chain risk.' Embraer signed a supply contract with Bharat Forge for forged raw materials — 'the deal supports supply chain diversification strategy focused on expanding global supplier base.' Aerospace exports scaled 4x in five years. Multiple new customer wins attributed to supply chain diversification.

govt_capex.evidence: FY25 consolidated defence revenue approximately ₹1,700 crore (~11% of consolidated revenue of ₹15,123 crore). Defence order book at ₹94 billion as of March 2025. Defence sector accounted for 70% of new order wins worth ₹69 billion in FY25.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is steel (not crude-linked). Steel prices are the key input cost driver. No specific crude-linked raw material percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Overseas subsidiaries in US and Europe provide natural hedge through local operations. Specific hedging policy for export receivables not separately disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Export business ~58% of standalone Indian operations revenue. FY25 consolidated revenue ₹15,123 crore. US OEMs 'largely indicated willingness to absorb any incremental tariff burden' on US exports, confirming USD-denominated revenue exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Bharat Forge is among 75 firms selected for incentives under PLI scheme for Automobile and Auto Components sector (budgetary outlay ₹25,938 crore, FY2023-24 to FY2027-28). Specific PLI-attributed revenue % not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Pidilite is a predominantly domestic India business (adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals). International subsidiaries contributed ~₹887 crore of ~₹13,400 crore total FY25 revenue (~6.6%). No China+1 or export diversification narrative present.

rural.evidence: Pidilite's 'Small Town Gold' initiative targets over 65,000 villages with populations under 10,000. Consumer & Bazaar segment (81% of revenue) includes rural distribution. No specific rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: B2B segment (~19% of revenue) includes construction chemicals used in infrastructure projects, benefiting from government capex. No specific government capex revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Pidilite has very low leverage — Debt/Equity ratio of 0.02x. Essentially debt-free. Minimal rate sensitivity on the liability side.

crude_exposure.evidence: Vinyl Acetate Monomer (VAM) is the key crude-linked raw material (used in Fevicol and adhesives). VAM prices averaged ~$100/tonne in Q3 FY25 and rose ~5% in Q4 FY25, causing 15.9% rise in overall raw material costs. Specific % of revenue not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International subsidiaries' revenue ~₹887 crore in FY25 (~6.6% of consolidated). Asia revenue +3% YoY; Middle East and Africa +11.1% YoY. Specific hedging policy not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Garware Hi-Tech Films is 'evaluating options for supply chain diversification, including potential arrangements in other countries' in response to tariff pressures. The company's vertically integrated 'chips-to-film' model is described as globally unique — 'when tariffs spike and supply chains fracture, integration becomes insurance.' Exports grew from 67% in FY23 to 77% in FY25. Supply chain diversification narrative present but no explicit 'China+1' framing.

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials PTA (purified terephthalic acid) and MEG (monoethylene glycol) are derived from crude oil. Garware's profitability is sensitive to crude oil price fluctuations. Specific % of revenue not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company has subsidiaries in US and UK for international operations. Specific hedging policy not disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports 77% of total gross sales in FY25. US/North America accounts for approximately 50% of total revenues. Distribution network spans 90+ countries with subsidiaries in US and UK.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin Point is a major pharma exporter focused on Latin America (~76% of revenue) and Africa (~6%), with growing US business (~18%). Operates primarily in semi-regulated emerging markets. No explicit China+1 supply chain diversification narrative found. Export growth is driven by market expansion in LatAm/Africa/US rather than manufacturing shift away from China.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Revenues substantially in USD and other foreign currencies given ~98% export orientation. Specific hedging policy not disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: Total FY25 revenue ₹2,034 crore: Latin America ~76% (~₹1,546 crore), Africa ~6% (~₹122 crore), US regulated markets ~18% (~₹366 crore), domestic India ~2%.

pli_scheme.evidence: Caplin Point operates primarily in semi-regulated and emerging markets (LatAm, Africa). No evidence of PLI beneficiary status.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports accounted for 88% of gross sales in FY25. Investor materials describe 'unprecedented capex plans to augment capacities besides preparing for growing opportunities arising due to China plus one factor.' Europe ~46% and Americas ~27% of total revenue reflect ongoing shift of regulated-market sourcing away from China. Company explicitly cited China+1 as driver of capacity expansion in niche APIs.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Divi's is net-cash / near-debt-free; specific floating rate liability % not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company uses chemical intermediates and solvents with indirect crude/petroleum linkage; specific % of revenue not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Standard practice includes natural hedge via export receivables; specific forward contract details not confirmed in accessible sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Europe 46% + Americas 27% = ~73% of total revenue in hard currency (USD/EUR). Company is a net exporter with near-zero net forex risk on a natural hedge basis.

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories qualifies under PLI scheme for Key Starting Materials (KSMs)/Drug Intermediates and APIs. India's bulk drug sector turned net exporter (₹2,280 crore surplus in FY2024-25) partly driven by PLI; Divi's is among the top beneficiaries. Specific PLI incentive as % of revenue not disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Radico Khaitan is an IMFL (Indian Made Foreign Liquor) company with ~91% domestic revenue. Exports (9-10% of revenue) go to 85+ countries but are opportunistic; no China+1 supply-chain diversification narrative present.

rural.evidence: Radico sells through state government-controlled distribution in India. Rural vs urban split not separately disclosed. Mass-market brands (8 PM, Old Admiral, Magic Moments) have significant rural/semi-urban presence. No specific rural revenue % reported.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt at FY25-end ~₹631 crore (down from ~₹885 crore in FY24, 46.8% decline in long-term debt). Company targets becoming near-debt-free by FY27. Specific floating vs fixed rate breakdown not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are ENA (Extra Neutral Alcohol from molasses/grain) and glass bottles/packaging. Glass and PET/packaging have indirect crude/energy linkage. Specific crude-linked raw material % not disclosed. Gross margins stable at ~43.6% in FY25.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Predominantly INR-denominated business. Hedging policy for 9-10% export revenue not explicitly described.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports ~9-10% of revenue across 85+ countries. Premium export brands include Rampur Single Malt Whisky sold in US, Europe, and Asia.

pli_scheme.evidence: Radico Khaitan is an IMFL/spirits company. PLI schemes do not apply to IMFL manufacturing.

china_plus_one.evidence: Siemens India is primarily a domestically-focused industrial conglomerate. Certain products are supplied into the global Siemens supply chain (~15% of revenue), but no explicit China+1 narrative is framed in investor communications.

govt_capex.evidence: Q4 FY2025 segment breakdown: Smart Infrastructure ₹2,725 crore (53% of revenue), Mobility ₹1,135 crore (22%), Digital Industries ₹1,065 crore (21%), Low Voltage Motors ₹273 crore (5%). Smart Infrastructure (power T&D) + Mobility (rail/metro) combined = ~75% of revenue, substantially government/infrastructure capex-linked. FY2025 demerger of Energy business to Siemens Energy India means current Siemens India is concentrated in these infra/govt segments.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Siemens India is net cash positive as of FY2024/FY2025. Floating rate debt % not applicable / not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Siemens India is a technology/engineering company. Raw material costs include steel, copper, electronics/semiconductors. Minimal direct crude exposure; specific % not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses natural hedging (imports for domestic manufacturing offset by exports). Formal hedging policy details not confirmed in accessible sources.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports constitute approximately 15% of revenue (supply into global Siemens supply chain). Majority of revenue is domestic INR-denominated.

pli_scheme.evidence: Siemens India operates in industrial automation, power infrastructure, and mobility. No PLI scheme participation confirmed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Nippon India AMC is a domestic asset management company. China+1 is not relevant to its business model.

rural.evidence: B-30 (Beyond Top 30 cities) AUM was ₹1.32 trillion = 19.8% of total NIMF AUM as of March 2025. B-30 AUM share is not equivalent to rural revenue %. Management fees proportional to AUM but rural/B-30 revenue % not separately disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nippon India AMC is near-debt-free. Interest rate sensitivity operates through AUM composition: rising rates can reduce equity AUM (49.8% of total AUM) and affect management fee revenue indirectly. Debt AUM benefits from rate cuts. No floating rate debt to disclose.

inr_exposure.evidence: Primarily INR-denominated management fees on domestic AUM (total ₹6.54 lakh crore). Offshore advisory mandates and GIFT City fund management generate some foreign currency revenue, but % not material and not separately disclosed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Nippon India AMC is a financial services / asset management company. PLI schemes do not apply to this sector.

china_plus_one.evidence: Varun Beverages is a PepsiCo franchisee for beverages. International operations are in South Asia (Nepal, Sri Lanka) and Africa (Zambia, Zimbabwe, Morocco, South Africa via BevCo acquisition, DRC, Tanzania, Ghana). China+1 narrative not applicable.

rural.evidence: VBL has aggressively expanded rural and semi-urban presence in India, adding over 100,000 new visi-coolers to deepen rural penetration. Rural expansion is a key strategic priority. Specific rural revenue % not disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Total debt ~₹2,508 crore. Cost of debt ~7.25%; interest coverage ratio ~11x. Specific floating vs fixed breakdown not disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: PET resin (for bottles) is a crude-linked key raw material at ~₹90-100/kg. Company setting up PET recycling JV with Indorama to fulfill 20-25% of PET requirements. Sugar is another major input. Specific crude-linked raw material % of revenue not disclosed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Active currency risk management mentioned for international operations. Specific instruments not disclosed.
inr_exposure.evidence: India contributed approximately 67% of revenues in CY2024; international operations (Africa + South Asia) ~33%. Africa revenue primarily in local currencies (ZAR, ZMW, etc.).

pli_scheme.evidence: Varun Beverages is a beverages/FMCG company (PepsiCo franchisee). No PLI scheme participation confirmed.
